back: One long DNA molecule wound around histone proteins; after replication, two sister chromatids joined at a centromere.
Non-coding repeated sequences at chromosome ends that are shortened at each replication instead of genes.
G1 (growth) → S (DNA replication) → G2 (preparation) → mitosis → cytokinesis.

front: What happens to DNA content in S phase?
back: It doubles: 1 unit → 2 units; each chromosome gets two chromatids.
Positively charged histones attract the negatively charged phosphate groups of DNA.
Toti: any cell incl. placenta (zygote). Pluri: almost any body cell (embryonic stem cells). Multi: a limited range (bone marrow).
Adds repeats to telomeres; active in stem cells, germ-line cells and most cancer cells.

front: Estimating phase duration from cell counts
back: Duration = (cells in phase ÷ total cells) × length of the cell cycle.
